citation: Wijekumar, K., Meyer, B. J. F., & Lei, P. (2017). Web-based text structure strategy instruction improves seventh graders' content area reading comprehension. Journal of Educational Psychology, 109(6), 741-760. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000168
report_number: DOI 10.1037/edu0000168; ERIC EJ1149967; funded by U.S. Department of Education, Institute of Education Sciences (IES efficacy/replication grant on the Intelligent Tutoring System for the Structure Strategy, ITSS, grades 4/5/7/8).
design: Multisite within-school cluster randomized controlled trial. In each of 25 rural/suburban schools, all 7th-grade language arts teachers (none declined) were randomly assigned at the teacher/classroom level to ITSS (intervention) or control. Result: 108 classrooms (59 ITSS / 49 control). Intervention = Intelligent Tutoring System for the Structure Strategy (ITSS), a web-based text-structure-strategy reading-comprehension program used 1-2 sessions/week, 30-45 min each, over a 6-7 month school year as a partial substitute for the standard language arts curriculum. TPD-FOR-CURRICULA component: intervention teachers received an approx. 3-hour teacher professional development session at the start of the year (description of the text structure strategy, how ITSS functions, typical student interactions); intervention teachers also got biweekly progress reports. Control = business-as-usual standard 7th-grade language arts curriculum, no ITSS. Subject = reading comprehension (-> Reading); grade 7 (registry grade band 7-12). Outcomes: GSRT (Gray Silent Reading Test, Wiederholt & Blalock 2000) = standardized DISTAL/independent reading-comprehension measure (Form B pretest, Form A posttest; publisher reliability alpha >= .97, study Cronbach alpha .88) -- this is the headline outcome for the primary research question; plus researcher-designed signaling/comparison/main-idea/problem-and-solution measures (developer-made proximal measures). Analytic sample 2,489 students; complete-case GSRT posttest n approx. 1,131 ITSS / 893 control. Impact estimated via three-level HLM (students in classrooms in schools), HLM7 software, main-effects model M1 with student- and class-level GSRT pretest, signaling pretest, gender, and school locale (rural) as covariates -> clustering accounted for. Pretest-adjusted (covariate-adjusted) impact estimates.
problems:
STUDY IDENTITY CONFIRMED: row 135 = Wijekumar, Meyer & Lei (2017), Journal of Educational Psychology, the large-scale grade-7 ITSS / Structure Strategy web-based READING-comprehension cluster RCT (DOI 10.1037/edu0000168). This is distinct from row 134 (Wijekumar et al. 2009 = CompassLearning Odyssey MATH NCEE report). Registry descriptors for row 135 (Teacher/Class RCT, grades 7-12, 'TPD for curricula') match this study (within-school teacher/classroom random assignment; grade 7; intervention teachers received PD to deliver the ITSS reading curriculum). Brief said likely grades 4-8 / J. Educational Psychology -- correct journal; the 2017 paper specifically is the grade-7 study.

LEGAL OA SOURCE: No direct full-text PDF was offered by OpenAlex/Unpaywall (publisher hybrid OA, no PDF URL). The PDF used is the OFFICIAL APA accepted-manuscript posting on PsycNet (https://psycnet.apa.org/manuscript/2017-11249-001.pdf), which is the publisher's own legal author-manuscript copy bearing the APA copyright/manuscript-version notice and the DOI. This is the accepted-manuscript (not copy-of-record) version; tables/numbers were extracted directly from it. No piracy sources used.

EFFECT-SIZE FOCUS: Per the meta-analysis (independent measures only) the qualifying TPD-vs-BAU student reading-achievement contrast is the STANDARDIZED GSRT (test_type=standardized_independent; outcome_role=primary; g=0.18). I also extracted the researcher-designed (developer-made, proximal) measures and labeled them test_type=researcher_made / outcome_role=secondary or subscale so central logic can filter them out -- they are NOT independent measures.

EFFECT-SIZE METHOD (authors, Table 2 note + Methods): ES = adjusted (for pretest + covariates) ITSS-minus-control group mean difference (HLM M1 coefficient for ITSS, coded ITSS=1/2, control=-1/2) divided by the UNADJUSTED pooled within-treatment-group STUDENT-LEVEL PRETEST standard deviation (WWC-recommended standardizer). For GSRT: d = 2.12 / 11.52 = 0.184 -> authors report 0.18. I applied Hedges' small-sample correction J = 1 - 3/(4*df - 1) using the reported df=80 (Table 2 note; level-2/classroom df): J=0.9906, g = 0.182. g_se = J*(SE_b / s) = 0.9906*(0.48/11.52) = 0.0413; g_var = 0.00170. All my computed g for the researcher-designed measures reproduce the authors' reported ES to 2 decimals.

CLUSTER/ICC: Impact SE comes from the three-level HLM, so it accounts for student-within-classroom-within-school clustering -> cluster_adjusted=true. Assignment unit = teacher/classroom (108 classrooms) nested in 25 schools; I record n_clusters=108 (classrooms, the randomization unit) and note 25 schools. ICC is NOT explicitly reported as an ICC; I computed design-effect ICCs from the M0 unconditional variance components in Table 3 (school=2.48, classroom=20.04, student=136.13; total=158.65): classroom-level ICC=0.126 (recorded, the relevant cluster level), school-level ICC=0.016. These are derived, not author-stated as ICCs.

NUMERIC NUANCE: GSRT adjusted coefficient 2.12 (SE .48) is stable across HLM models M1/M2/M3/M5 (only M4 with locale interaction differs slightly at 2.01). I used M1 (the main-effects model the authors used for the primary question and effect sizes).

effect_sizes.arm_label: ITSS (Intelligent Tutoring System for the Structure Strategy; web-based text-structure-strategy reading-comprehension curriculum) + ~3-hour teacher PD vs business-as-usual standard 7th-grade language arts curriculum
effect_sizes.test_name: Gray Silent Reading Test (GSRT; Wiederholt & Blalock, 2000); standardized distal reading-comprehension measure; Form B pretest, Form A posttest
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of school year; single 6-7 month 2014-15-era intervention year)
effect_sizes.g_method: Pretest/covariate-adjusted standardized mean difference per the authors (Table 2 note): numerator = HLM main-effects model M1 fixed-effect coefficient for ITSS = 2.12 GSRT scale points (SE 0.48, p<.001, df=80; Table 2 & Table 3 M1 column), adjusting for student- and class-level GSRT pretest, signaling pretest, gender, and rural locale. Standardizing SD = unadjusted pooled within-treatment-group STUDENT-LEVEL PRETEST SD of GSRT = 11.52 (Table 2; WWC-recommended standardizer). d = 2.12/11.52 = 0.184, matching the authors' reported ES 0.18. Hedges J = 1 - 3/(4*80 - 1) = 0.9906 -> g = 0.182. g_se = J*(0.48/11.52) = 0.0413; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.00170. SE is from the three-level HLM so it already accounts for clustering (cluster_adjusted=true). Posttest student-level descriptive means/SDs (Table 1, raw/unadjusted): ITSS 40.02 (SD 11.66, n=1,131), control 37.42 (SD 13.47, n=893); these are unadjusted and are recorded for reference only -- g uses the adjusted impact 2.12 / pretest SD 11.52.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 2 (GSRT coefficient 2.12, SE 0.48, pooled pretest SD 11.52, ES 0.18; df=80); Table 3 M1 column (ITSS=2.12, SE .48) and M0 variance components (school 2.48 / classroom 20.04 / student 136.13); Table 1 (GSRT student-level posttest: ITSS n=1,131 M=40.02 SD=11.66; control n=893 M=37.42 SD=13.47); Methods (effect-size definition; GSRT standardized-test description; 108 classrooms / 25 schools / 2,489 students; teacher-level random assignment).
effect_sizes.notes: PRIMARY and the only INDEPENDENT/standardized reading-achievement contrast in this report -- the headline outcome for the study's primary research question. ITSS classrooms scored ~0.18 SD higher on the GSRT than BAU control, statistically significant (p<.001). Intent-to-treat-style full sample (students using ITSS <=30 min total over the year were excluded a priori, mostly pull-out special-ed students, with matched exclusion in control). cluster_adjusted=true (HLM SE). icc=0.126 is the classroom-level ICC derived from M0 variance components (school-level ICC=0.016); randomization unit was teacher/classroom (108 classrooms in 25 schools), so n_clusters=108. The researcher-designed measures below are developer-made (researcher_made) proximal outcomes and are NOT independent measures.
